why: The Aleph protocol said 'dedup, rank by agreement' and left the merge to a human.
Three lenses describing the same defect in three vocabularies cannot be compared by
string match, so agreement was judgement, and judgement does not survive a stall.
This is the shared vocabulary. Every aleph MUST return one of these keys. Agreement
then becomes arithmetic: how many distinct lenses named the same key on the same
surface. A key is a DEFECT CLASS, never a fix and never a score.
rule: Add a key only when a real finding has nowhere to go. Never rename one - the ledger
keys findings by it, and a rename orphans history. Retire with 'retired': true.

severity.blocker: the surface cannot ship: a floor is broken or the thing does not work
severity.major: ships, but a stated studio or learning goal is not met
severity.minor: real, worth fixing, costs nothing to carry one more release

floor.note: mechanical, gate-owned. A non-L1 lens naming one of these is a TOOL BLIND SPOT.

items.CONTRAST-FLOOR: text under 4.5:1 in any comfort stop
items.TYPE-FLOOR: rendered text under the 18px absolute floor
items.DARK-MISSING: no dark palette; the OS will force-darken unmeasured
items.OFFLINE-BROKEN: loads anything external; the single-file offline floor is broken
items.FOCUS-INVISIBLE: keyboard focus has no visible ring
items.NAV-MISSING: a screen without both back and home
items.EMOJI: decorative emoji anywhere on the surface
items.JS-ERROR: an uncaught exception fires during play
items.DEAD-CONTROL: a control that changes nothing when used
items.DEAD-END: a state with no live control and no end signal
items.H-OVERFLOW: the page scrolls sideways at phone width; content runs off the screen
items.OUTLINE-BROKEN: a labelled region points at an id that does not exist, or a screen carries no heading, so assistive tech is handed an empty outline exactly where the player is. Added 2026-08-07: L3 found it on the-tell.html and correctly reported that it had nowhere to go.
items.FOCUS-LOST: after a transition focus lands on a hidden element or drops to body, so the next Tab restarts from the top of the document (WCAG 2.2 focus order)

items.OPENING-WALL: the first thing is text or settings, not the scene
items.INSTRUCTION-WALL: directions stacked above the first control; the player must read before they may act. Founder-named 2026-08-07: 'a wall of directions that were irrelevant and unreadable for my phone.' Measured in words-above-first-action at 390px, chrome excluded.
items.ACTION-BELOW-FOLD: the first thing you can do is more than one screen down at phone width
items.INVITATION-UNCLEAR: zero or more than one co-equal primary invitation on entry
items.FTUE-UNGUIDED: a first-time player cannot tell what to do without being told
items.FEEDBACK-ABSENT: an action produces no visible reaction
items.GAME-FEEL-DISPLACED: the reaction paints somewhere other than where the action happened
items.PROGRESS-ILLEGIBLE: the player cannot tell where they are or how much is left
items.FAIL-STATE-PUNITIVE: being wrong costs progress instead of teaching
items.REPLAY-BLOCKED: the player cannot try again without reloading

items.VALUE-PROP-BURIED: what this is and why it matters is not in the first screen
items.TEXT-WALL: prose where an image or an interaction should carry the idea
items.READABILITY-HIGH: reading level above the stated audience
items.DISCLOSURE-DUMP: everything at once; nothing held back until asked for
items.LABEL-AMBIGUOUS: a control whose label does not predict what it does
items.SOURCE-UNNAMED: a factual claim with no provenance. Studio floor: a number with no source is a rumour.

items.IMAGE-FLOOR: screen is under 50% image (founder canon C7)
items.COMPOSITION-UNRESOLVED: no focal path; the eye has nowhere to land first
items.PALETTE-INCOHERENT: colour does not read as one system across the surface
items.TYPE-HIERARCHY-FLAT: everything is the same weight; nothing is ranked
items.ART-PLACEHOLDER: scaffolding art still in place where authored art was intended
items.VOICE-NOT-FOUNDER: copy that is machine-generic rather than the founder's own

learning.note: added 2026-08-07. Nothing in the studio assessed this before, on teaching games.

items.OUTCOME-UNMAPPED: no stated competency or iSLO the build is aimed at
items.OBJECTIVE-IMPLICIT: the learner cannot tell what they are meant to come away with
items.COGNITIVE-LOAD-EXTRANEOUS: effort spent on the interface or decoration rather than the idea (Mayer, coherence)
items.SPLIT-ATTENTION: text and the thing it describes are separated in space or time
items.PRACTICE-ABSENT: the learner reads or watches but never retrieves or produces
items.FEEDBACK-UNINFORMATIVE: right or wrong with no why; nothing to act on
items.FEEDBACK-DELAYED: the response arrives too late to attach to the move that earned it
items.TRANSFER-UNSUPPORTED: one context only; nothing varies, so nothing generalises
items.ASSESSMENT-MISALIGNED: what gets scored is not what was taught (constructive alignment)
items.MISCONCEPTION-UNADDRESSED: the common wrong answer is never surfaced or corrected
items.AGENCY-ABSENT: no choice that changes anything; the learner is a reader, not an actor
items.RUBRIC-UNLINKED: a scored activity whose criteria are never shown to the learner
